---
title: "Results: In-silico Performance Validation"
---

This section validates the designed primer/probe sets in silico across the **three design databases** — `indo-only`, `sea-only`, and `all-partial` — evaluated on the same global surveillance set (Flu A MP: $N=50{,}750$; Flu B MP: $N=7{,}248$). `indo-only` remains the main design thread of this report; the other two are shown for comparison. The full head-to-head trade-off (safety, multiplex, thermodynamics) is on the [Design DB Comparison](results_design_comparison.qmd) page.

::: {.callout-important title="Compare scenarios on PCR; read RAA per-scenario"}
Cross-scenario numbers are only fair on the **PCR** lens — every build uses the same `seqkit -m 3` PCR model. The **RAA** figures are **not** directly comparable across scenarios: the `indo-only` run predates the M10 RAA decoupling fix, so its RAA is **PCR-capped** (it can never exceed PCR — e.g. global A/H5N1 reads 31.84%), whereas `sea-only` and `all-partial` were run with the decoupled model (RAA can exceed PCR). The decoupled RAA-viable estimate for `indo-only` comes from the seqkit-free M12 attribution (global A/H5N1 ≈ 94%). `indo-only` has not been re-run under the new model (HPC capacity). Rankings below are therefore made on PCR; RAA is shown per-scenario with this caveat.
:::

---

## 1. Overall In-Silico Coverage and Degeneracy Uplift

IUPAC degenerate bases were verified by evaluating each candidate in two forms — **degenerate** (as designed) and **non-degenerate** (degenerate positions collapsed to consensus). Degenerate coverage of the rank-1 candidate on the global set:

**Flu A MP** ($N=50{,}750$):

| Design DB | PCR non-degen | **PCR degenerate** | RAA detected (see caveat) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `indo-only` | 18.61% | **91.20%** | 91.16% † |
| `sea-only` | 80.89% | **95.68%** | 62.07% |
| `all-partial` | 19.22% | **93.88%** | 95.12% |

**Flu B MP** ($N=7{,}248$):

| Design DB | PCR non-degen | **PCR degenerate** | RAA detected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `indo-only` | 83.22% | **83.22%** | 83.22% † |
| `sea-only` | 83.29% | **99.68%** | 99.81% |
| `all-partial` | 83.29% | **99.68%** | 99.81% |

† `indo-only` RAA is PCR-capped (old M10) — not comparable to the decoupled sea/all-partial RAA; see the caveat above.

### Key findings

*   **Degeneracy is essential**: collapsing degenerate bases to consensus drops `indo-only` Flu A PCR coverage from **91.20% to 18.61%** (>70 pp), confirming IUPAC bases are needed to absorb natural variation [@elnifro2000; @khan2020]. `all-partial` shows the same collapse (93.88% → 19.22%); `sea-only`'s non-degen floor is higher (80.89%) because its consensus already matches a broader regional set.
*   **On PCR, a broader database raises Flu B but is mixed for Flu A**: Flu B PCR jumps from 83.22% (`indo-only`) to 99.68% (`sea-only`/`all-partial`). For Flu A the overall PCR is similar (91–96%), but the *per-subtype* picture (§3) is where the databases diverge.

## 3. Subtype-Specific Performance (global set, Flu A)

The clearest view of how the design database matters is the **global per-subtype PCR-amplified** coverage (fair across scenarios — same seqkit model):

| Subtype | N | `indo-only` PCR | `sea-only` PCR | `all-partial` PCR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A / H3N2 | 19,258 | **99.01%** | 97.87% | 93.81% |
| A / H1N1 | 18,468 | 96.92% | **99.15%** | 97.10% |
| A / H9N2 | 4,315 | 91.24% | 77.87% | **98.49%** |
| A / H5N1 | 1,784 | **31.84%** | **96.69%** | 79.54% |

*   **`indo-only`** is strongest on the human-seasonal subtypes it was built around (H3N2 99.0%, H1N1 96.9%) but weakest on **global A/H5N1 (31.84%)** — its Indonesia-tuned primers miss divergent avian H5N1 at the strict `≤3`-mismatch PCR gate. Under RAA tolerance this gap largely closes (M12 estimate ≈ 94%; see the Module 10 page §1.3), so it is a strict-PCR/importation signal, not a routine-use hole.
*   **A broader database buys H5N1 breadth**: `sea-only` (96.69%) and `all-partial` (79.54%) PCR-amplify far more global H5N1 than `indo-only`, at a modest cost to H3N2 (`all-partial` 93.81%). This is the core database trade-off.

::: {.callout-note title="Design/focal-DB coverage (context)"}
On the **focal DB it was built on**, `indo-only` reaches $>96\%$ on every major subtype (A/H5N1 98.72% n=312, A/H3N2 99.58% n=238, A/H1N1 96.25% n=160) — the design covers what circulates locally. The focal-DB per-subtype tables for `sea-only`/`all-partial` are dominated by their own (regional / avian-heavy) training composition and are not directly comparable, so the global table above is used for the cross-scenario view.
:::

---

## 4. Temporal Robustness & Antigenic Drift (`indo-only`)

Breaking the `indo-only` degenerate coverage down by collection year (M10 `breakdowns.year`) shows how the recommended design tracks viral evolution on the global set:

*   Coverage is **not flat**: high-80s to low-90s for most years (2015 87.4%, 2016 89.0%, 2017 88.8%, 2018 88.1%, 2019 93.7%), a low of **74.4% in 2020**, then recovery to 2023 92.8%, 2024 93.4%, **2025 96.7%**.
*   The 2020 trough coincides with the pandemic-era collapse in influenza sampling (1,393 sequences that year) and a lineage shift; recovery to >93% shows the **187–341 bp** target stays well matched to 2023–2025 strains.
*   These per-year figures are PCR (the fair lens); RAA-viable coverage in divergent years is higher (M12).
